# Nehemiah Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 472v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Those who sealed the agreement were: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,

**2** along with the following priests: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, **3** Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, **4** Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, **5** Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, **6** Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, **7** Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, **8** Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.

**9** The Levites who signed: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the clan of Henadad, and Kadmiel; **10** along with their associates: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan, **11** Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, **12** Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah, **13** Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.

**14** The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani, **15** Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, **16** Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, **17** Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, **18** Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai, **19** Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai, **20** Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, **21** Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, **22** Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, **23** Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub, **24** Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, **25** Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, **26** Ahiah, Hanan, Anan, **27** Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

**28** The rest of the people also committed themselves — the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and everyone who had separated from the surrounding peoples to follow the Law of God, along with their wives, sons, and daughters — everyone mature enough to understand.

**29** They joined with their leaders in taking a solemn oath, binding themselves under a curse to follow the Law of God given through his servant Moses, and to obey carefully all the commands, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD our God.

**30** Specifically, we pledged:

We will not let our daughters marry people from the surrounding nations, and we will not let our sons marry their daughters.

**31** When merchants from other nations bring goods or grain to sell on the Sabbath, we will refuse to buy. We will observe the sabbatical year by letting the land rest and canceling all debts.

**32** We accept the responsibility of contributing one-third of a shekel each year for the upkeep of the house of our God —

**33** to pay for the bread set out before God, the regular grain offerings and burnt offerings, the Sabbath and new moon observances, the annual festivals, the sacred offerings, the sin offerings to atone for Israel, and all the other operations of God's house.

**34** We — priests, Levites, and people — have cast lots to determine when each ancestral family will bring wood for the altar of the LORD our God at designated times throughout the year, as the Law requires.

**35** We commit to bringing the firstfruits of our crops and the firstfruits of every fruit tree to the LORD's house each year.

**36** As the Law prescribes, we will bring the firstborn of our sons and our livestock — the firstborn of our herds and flocks — to God's house, to the priests who serve there.

**37** We will bring the best of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, new wine, and olive oil to the priests in the storerooms of God's house. We will bring a tenth of our produce to the Levites, who collect tithes in all the towns where we work.

**38** A priest from Aaron's line must be present when the Levites collect tithes. The Levites must then bring a tenth of the tithes up to God's house, to the storerooms of the treasury.

**39** The people of Israel and the Levites are to bring their contributions of grain, new wine, and oil to the storerooms where the sacred vessels are kept and where the priests, gatekeepers, and singers serve. We will not neglect the house of our God.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes
1. **Covenant as community constitution** — This is not merely a religious ceremony but a social contract. The covenant addresses intermarriage, Sabbath commerce, temple economics, and agricultural tithes — touching every dimension of communal life. Faith and daily practice are inseparable.
2. **The one-third shekel** — The reduction from the Torah's half-shekel temple tax reveals the economic reality behind the spiritual commitment: this impoverished community is doing what it can, not what ideal circumstances would require. Grace meets reality.
3. **"We will not neglect"** — The chapter ends with a promise that becomes tragically ironic when read alongside chapter 13, where nearly every commitment made here is broken. The gap between covenant promise and lived reality is one of the Hebrew Bible's most honest and recurring themes.

*— PNEUMA*
